correctness.rationale: For two connected seven-vertex simple motifs the exact selectors δ₂=(0,0,1,1,0,0,0) and δ₃=(1,1,1,1,1,1,0) annihilate polynomial eigenvectors v₂(λ), v₃(λ) at every root of p₂=x²+x−4 and p₃=x³+x²−4x−2. Direct independent SymPy matrix calculations verified (A_H−xI)v≡0 modulo the irreducible minimal polynomial, δ·v≡0, nonzero v, and divisor in the motif characteristic polynomial; the periodic Floquet perturbation (z+z⁻¹)δδᵀ hence leaves a compact eigenfunction supported on one cell. Discriminants 17 and 316 and gcd=1 give five distinct real values. Every six-cell compact eigenfunction would require an eigenvalue of its induced simple six-vertex adjacency matrix. Independent exact charpoly enumeration of all 156 unlabeled simple six-vertex graphs (including disconnected) found zero divisible by p₂ or p₃, proving the finite minimality exclusion exhaustively.
residual_risks: The 156-graph search is exhaustive only of finite simple unweighted six-vertex adjacency graphs, and is not an infinite periodic-graph census.
Claim concerns single-cell support, not all flat bands or all F7 energies.

value.rationale: The exact first failure of a specifically published odd/even spectral-set conjectural equality is a motivated mathematical counterexample and sharp finite obstruction. Two small connected periodic motifs plus a complete 156-class lower-size exclusion give five exact algebraic witnesses. The finite classification is substantive because it settles the complete six-cell boundary for those roots, not an arbitrary small census.
residual_risks: The witness set is a subset of F7−F6, not its full enumeration.

limitations: Finite enumeration is exhaustive for all simple six-vertex motifs and valid as finite negative certificate; not claimed to classify all periodic graphs.
